question: According to the abstract of Xu (2010), the CQ algorithm of Byrne is shown to be a special case of which type of algorithm in convex minimization, and what convergence property does it have in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces?

In Xu (2010)'s Theorem 3.1, what upper bound (in terms of the largest eigenvalue L or the norm of A) must the relaxation parameter gamma satisfy for the CQ algorithm to converge weakly to a solution of the SFP?
According to Proposition 2.2 in Xu (2010), what two properties do both the projection P_K and its complement I - P_K have?
In Byrne (2002)'s Algorithm 1.1, what is the exact iterative update formula for x^(k+1) in the CQ algorithm?
According to Byrne (2002), what quantity does L denote in the condition gamma in (0, 2/L), and what property of the matrix does it come from?
According to Byrne (2002)'s abstract, which well-known image reconstruction technique is identified as a particular case of a block-iterative version of the CQ algorithm?
According to the abstract of Xu et al. (2018), what optimization principle from computational statistics do the authors use to generalize the CQ algorithm to nonlinear split feasibility problems?
In Xu et al. (2018), what nonlinear mapping h(x1, x2) is used as the motivating toy example in section 2.1 to illustrate the MM algorithm?
According to Xu et al. (2018), what technique is highlighted as one of two application domains for their case study, alongside liver cancer?
Trong bài của Xu (2010), dãy lặp sinh bởi thuật toán CQ hội tụ yếu về nghiệm của bài toán SFP khi nào (điều kiện về tham số gamma)?
What does Byrne (2002) identify as the main computational burden avoided by the CQ algorithm, compared to earlier iterative methods for the SFP that required computing an inverse operator?
What acceleration technique, based on approximating curvature from differences between iterates rather than computing the full Hessian, do Xu et al. (2018) apply to speed up their MM algorithm?
Theo Xu (2010), phep chieu P_K va phan bu cua no co tinh chat gi dac biet duoc neu trong Menh de 2.2 (lien quan den tinh khong gian)?

Compare the setting in which Byrne (2002) originally proves convergence of the CQ algorithm with the setting Xu (2010) extends it to. What is the key dimensional difference, and how does it affect the convergence result (norm vs weak convergence)?

Byrne (2002) and Xu (2010) both assume the split feasibility problem's constraint map is linear (h(x) = Ax). How does Xu et al. (2018) extend this framework, and what tool from computational statistics do they use to handle the resulting non-convexity?

All three papers (Byrne 2002, Xu 2010, Xu et al. 2018) build on the CQ algorithm. Which of the three papers proves convergence using fixed-point / averaged-mapping / nonexpansive-operator arguments, and which instead uses a majorization-minimization / surrogate-function argument?
Both Byrne (2002) and Xu (2010) discuss special cases of the CQ algorithm for solving linear equations Ax = b. Name the classical iterative method that both papers identify as such a special case.

Trong ba tai lieu, ai la tac gia de xuat dung nguyen ly majorization-minimization (MM) de mo rong thuat toan CQ sang anh xa phi tuyen, va bai do xuat ban nam nao? (Luu y: co hai tac gia khac nhau cung ho 'Xu' trong bo tai lieu nay.)

Dinh ly 2.1 trong bai cua Byrne (2002) phat bieu dieu gi ve su hoi tu cua day {x^k} sinh boi thuat toan CQ? (Luu y: ca Byrne 2002 va Xu 2010 deu co mot 'Theorem' ve hoi tu CQ danh so gan giong nhau - can xac dinh dung nguon.)
Bai bao nao la bai GOC dau tien de xuat thuat toan CQ (khong phai bai mo rong/relax no)?
